about: Every friction a person meets in the apps, in our own words: where, what happened, the fix, and its state. Principle ask-by-frequency (owner, 2026-11-11). The number of open items only goes down; governance/tests/test_frictions.py holds the shape.

frictions.where: Life OS, Setup (edit profile)
frictions.friction: Editing the profile showed no children or loans, and saving erased them, so the Kids tab asked for the child again
frictions.fix: Setup reloads children and loans when editing (PR 233)

frictions.where: Life OS, Career
frictions.friction: Asked again for take-home, gross, spending, savings, investments, birth month and retirement age
frictions.fix: Reads the profile and writes an edit back (PR 233)

frictions.where: Life OS, Life Map
frictions.friction: Asked again for ages, income, net worth and emergency fund
frictions.fix: Derives ages from birth dates and reads money from the profile (PR 233)

frictions.where: Life OS, Kids
frictions.friction: An empty 'Add your child' form beside the children already saved
frictions.fix: The add form is folded under 'Add another child' (PR 233)

frictions.where: Life OS, Setup (edit profile)
frictions.friction: Updating one changing number (investments) meant scrolling past name, birth date, city and family every time
frictions.fix: Editing the profile folds name, birth date, place, family and vision under two lines that show them; the money fields stay in view (test43)

frictions.where: Life OS
frictions.friction: No quick way to update the numbers that change (investments, savings, spending, loan balance) without opening the whole set-up
frictions.fix: A 'My numbers' card on Money and the Life Map: investments, savings, spending, take-home, saved to the profile with 'updated N days ago'; Career and the Life Map follow (test43). The monthly cue is the existing Money Date ritual

frictions.where: Life OS, Life Map
frictions.friction: Ages that come from birth dates still show as fields to type
frictions.fix: Ages from birth dates show as text with 'from your profile' (test43)

frictions.where: Life OS, Ops (Who touched my data)
frictions.friction: A backup saved the whole life as a readable file in Downloads, and the log screen showed a terminal command and a cramped four-column table on a phone
frictions.fix: Backups are encrypted by default with a backup phrase made once and kept on the device (shown once, in Settings any time); restore on a new device with the phrase; a readable copy only by name and flagged in red with what to delete; the log reads as plain rows with no command (test44, threat model lifeos-backup)

frictions.where: Life OS, Ops (CSV, spouse emergency page)
frictions.friction: The Excel (CSV) export and the spouse emergency page are still readable files
frictions.fix: Both are readable on purpose (for Excel, for a spouse in an emergency); show a one-line warning and log them in Who touched my data; consider a print-only emergency page

frictions.where: Life OS, Today
frictions.friction: Below the one action, about seven insight cards and five tall habit cards competed; nag titles (No OKRs set, No live commitment contract), citations and jargon, zero streaks and loud FLOOR TODAY pills read as guilt; Reset all data sat in red on the daily screen
frictions.fix: Habits as compact rows (floor shown, the IF-THEN folded under How, streak only when above zero); insights folded under one Insights (n) line and worded as optional invitations; reset moved to Ops as Erase all data on this device (test45; built by the open models, reviewed)

frictions.where: Life OS, Ops (backup buttons)
frictions.friction: Erase all data sat in the same row as Save backup, one tap away, and seven buttons of equal weight left the person to choose
frictions.fix: One primary (Save encrypted backup), Restore beside it, the rare exports folded under More backup options, and erase moved to a closed Danger zone at the bottom of Ops behind a typed ERASE, offering a backup first; erase now removes every value of this app (it used to remove three keys) and never another app's (test46)

frictions.where: Life OS, every screen that shows the profile
frictions.friction: Markup in the partner, child, loan or dream fields (from a restored file or another device) ran as code on four screens
frictions.fix: The profile is cleaned at the one read/write door; a fuzz of every tab and 85 typed fields runs nothing (test47)

frictions.where: Life OS, restore from file, OneDrive and move
frictions.friction: Three restore paths overwrote everything with one tap and no way back; a backup also carried its own old undo slot
frictions.fix: Every restore takes an undo snapshot first (30 minutes) and never restores the undo slot (test47)

frictions.where: Life OS, Inbox and Ask
frictions.friction: Terminal commands (./securax up, ./securax lifeos docs) shown on a phone screen
frictions.fix: Plain words (START-HERE on your laptop); the papers command folded under How, on the laptop (test47)

frictions.where: Life OS, Ops and Plan
frictions.friction: Three gold or primary buttons competed on Ops (check-in, backup, install) and Plan (three Adopt as OKR)
frictions.fix: One gold action on Ops (backup); install hidden once installed; Plan buttons quiet and plainly worded (test47)

frictions.where: Life OS, Map, Pillars, Scorecard, Plan, Career, Money, Book, Commit
frictions.friction: Unexplained jargon (KPI, OKR, FI, KGI, CSP) and shouting capitals (NORTH STAR, PROTECT, DOUBLES) found by the 360 scan
frictions.fix: Plain words with a gloss on first use, sentence case; built by the open models in one slice, reviewed (test48)

frictions.where: Life OS, Wheel, Ask, Commit, Life Map, Career
frictions.friction: Twelve inputs had no name a screen reader can read (the eight Wheel sliders, the estate address and key, the commitment deadline, a Life Map field), and a Career row nested a control inside a button
frictions.fix: aria-labels in plain words; the Career row is one real button (test49; axe: 0 violations on every tab; built by the open models)

frictions.where: Life OS, out-of-storage alert
frictions.friction: The alert sent the person to an Export backup button that no longer exists
frictions.fix: It names the current Save encrypted backup button (test49)

frictions.where: Vantage (every kit app), Wheel: Score each area
frictions.friction: Area names stacked one letter per line, because every select is 100% wide and took the whole row; no audit measured it
frictions.fix: Kit rows give a control only the room it needs and text at least 8 characters; a squashed-text rule in the shared UI rules now runs in the kit, Life OS and site audits (it flags the old page, passes the fixed one); test_squashed_text_is_measured_and_rows_give_text_room

frictions.where: Life OS, every tab (H1-H3 on Optionality and about 40 more)
frictions.friction: Short codes (H1-H3, L0-L4, S1-S5, Q1-Q4, NPS, PPF, EPF, EMI, CTC, PAN, CAS, CISO, OPSEC...) had no explanation a phone can show; H1-H3 lived only in a hover tooltip
frictions.fix: H1-H3 read Now, 1-2 years, 3-5 years; every code has a tap-to-explain glossary entry (test51; built by the open models)

frictions.where: Life OS, Pillars
frictions.friction: Cards showed built-in example values (sleep 6/10, family 4 hours, network 5) as if the person had entered them; Global Network appeared twice; about 30 red START HERE pills; units like str and ppl
frictions.fix: An unfilled card shows a dash and Tap to add yours; Contacts abroad and Professional network; quiet Not started; units in words; Plan steps ticked (test52; built by the open models)

frictions.where: Life OS, Pillars
frictions.friction: The progress bar blends the number with the plan steps ticked, so Debt avalanche 100% shows a half bar
frictions.fix: Show the number and the plan steps as two separate bars, or explain the blend in one line; it feeds the scores, so decide with the owner

frictions.where: Life OS, Wheel of Life
frictions.friction: Every unscored area read as 5, and eight sliders gave nothing to anchor a score on
frictions.fix: Unscored areas show as gaps; a measured score from the person's own numbers beside each area that has data; one-tap 1-10 (44 px targets); a gentle line where felt and measured differ by 3; last scored and a quarterly rhythm (test54; built by the open models, reviewed)

frictions.where: Life OS, Map (antifragility card) and section headings
frictions.friction: The hero card read flat (navy into navy) and headings were tiny tracked-out capitals
frictions.fix: A layered navy to midnight-teal gradient with a soft glow in the band colour over a solid navy fallback; sentence-case headings at a readable size; the contrast audit now layers a see-through glow over the element colour instead of stopping at it (test55)

frictions.where: Life OS, Ask (on a phone)
frictions.friction: One-time connection setup (gateway address, key, launch links) and two rare tools sat in plain view around the question box; on a phone the address field looked like something to fill in daily
frictions.fix: Question first; one plain status line (Ready, or Needs your laptop running: Set up once); rare tools under More tools; the connection folded at the bottom as Connection (set once) (test70)

frictions.where: Life OS, Shield
frictions.friction: No protection check for the car or two-wheeler, although a lapsed third-party cover is an offence with an unlimited liability
frictions.fix: A Vehicles entry among the vital few with six checks

frictions.where: Life OS, More sheet
frictions.friction: Twenty-three equal tiles; nothing says what matters first, so focus is lost
frictions.fix: The vital few first, ordered by risk (Shield, Deadlines, Systems, Money Map, Breaks, Wheel); everything else folded (test71)

frictions.where: Life OS, every screen with folded sections
frictions.friction: Any change redrew the screen and closed every open section, so the person reopened it and found their place again after each edit
frictions.fix: The render loop remembers the open sections and the scroll on the same tab and restores them; a newly opened tab still starts folded (test73)

frictions.where: Life OS, Ops, NIST CSF self-score
frictions.friction: A bare 0-5 slider per area with no meaning for each number
frictions.fix: Four plain choices per area (Not yet, Started, Mostly, Done and tested) and a one-line intro (test73)

frictions.where: Life OS: Stack, Shield checklists, CSF self-score
frictions.friction: The same fact (password manager, two-factor, tested backups, a will, insurance) had to be ticked separately in several places
frictions.fix: One store of shared facts; the latest tick anywhere shows everywhere, unticking anywhere is the override, and the CSF score follows the facts unless set by hand (test74)

frictions.where: Life OS: pillar detail, OKR key results (CSF already fixed)
frictions.friction: Sliders asked the person to drag a value the app could count from the checklist below it, or a bare 0-1 fraction with no meaning
frictions.fix: Checklist values count themselves; numeric measures get a number box with - and +; key results get five plain choices; no slider left (test75)

frictions.where: Life OS on Android, reinstalling the app for a new icon
frictions.friction: Removing the installed app can offer to delete its data; the owner could not remember the choice and the only copy was in the browser
frictions.fix: A gentle automatic weekly encrypted backup to the device (and OneDrive when connected), and a one-line reminder to back up before reinstalling

frictions.where: Life OS Goals tab
frictions.friction: The same suggested objective could be adopted twice, so two identical objectives sat side by side
frictions.fix: Adopting an objective you already have opens it instead; an exact, untouched copy is merged once

frictions.where: Life OS Risk tab
frictions.friction: Every risk not started read 'Exposed' in red with 0%, a wall of alarm that makes people look away
frictions.fix: Not started reads calm; one card says Start here (health first); red stays for real alarms

frictions.where: Life OS section titles, risk cards, OKR stages, spending bars
frictions.friction: Five emoji styles, chunky pill rows, a coloured Delete beside the safe button and an off-palette blue bar looked cheap next to the rest
frictions.fix: Gold-engraved medallions, one segmented control, a quiet labelled Delete away from the safe button, the healthy band drawn on the bar

frictions.where: Life OS in Hindi, Marathi and Gujarati
frictions.friction: Only about 63% of visible text was translated, and sentence fragments were translated piece by piece, so screens mixed two languages and read as inaccurate; there was no Gujarati and no way to hear a screen
frictions.fix: Gujarati for the vital few (Today 87%), a glossary and a quality gate, Listen in the person's language; fragments to templates and full coverage next (queue i18n-quality)

frictions.where: Life OS, the first minutes and every day
frictions.friction: Method words (the floor, one open action, L0 Identity, vital few, Prime Directive, Runway) and four typed money questions made even the owner too tired to start; a just-finished set-up showed 'Buffer low' for a number never asked
frictions.fix: Plain English on screen with the research kept underneath, four questions answered by taps, and nothing called low that the app does not know

frictions.where: Life OS daily question, Goals heading, Inbox, More menu, Career
frictions.friction: An unclear cash question, a doubled heading ('Quarterly Quarter goals'), an Inbox that opened on a paragraph, a type choice, a tax-paper list and eight reviews of up to 240 minutes, tabs for children or vehicles the person said they do not have, and no way to weigh an offer abroad
frictions.fix: Plain question, the heading fixed and every screen scanned for doubled words, No hides what cannot apply, the Inbox opens on one box with the rest folded, offers abroad weighed in usable rupees

frictions.where: Life OS scores and the Integrations copy-in boxes
frictions.friction: A friend's test: the person scores their own life, which drifts from reality, and copying numbers in by hand each month is heavy.
frictions.fix: Share or paste an EPFO, bank, card-bill, NPS or fund message: the Life OS reads the amount on the device and saves it dated, with one tap; net worth then comes from the statements. Next: exercise from the Move ticks' minutes, and a fund statement PDF shared straight in.

frictions.where: Money
frictions.friction: With six or more credit cards, a person does not know which to use when, and loses rewards and interest-free days.
frictions.fix: Which card, when, and where your money went: cards found by themselves in pasted or shared bank messages (no typing); from each card's name and statement day only, the big-spend card of the day (most days before paying), one card per category, and the three habits that matter more than rewards.

frictions.where: Phone alerts (ntfy) and bank messages arriving by themselves (SMS forwarder)
frictions.friction: To get alerts or automatic bank messages a person must install and configure another app, copy a token and type an estate address; nobody but an engineer will.
frictions.fix: Zero-setup paths: alerts by the Life OS own web push (one Allow tap); bank and card alerts read from the e-mail inbox the person already signs in with (one consent tap, read-only, only bank senders); the share sheet stays the one-tap fallback; pairing by one QR scan. The forwarder and ntfy stay only as folded owner-engineer options.

frictions.where: Set-up of the gateway, sync, inbox, alerts and the cloud sessions
frictions.friction: The owner is asked again and again to copy tokens, keys and credentials into several places (.env lines, phone apps, settings forms); keeping them in step is almost impossible.
frictions.fix: One secret store on the estate makes every token itself (./securax up creates any that are missing) and is the only place one lives; a device gets what it needs by the pairing QR scan or the one-door sign-in; every guide and command stops printing a step that asks the person to paste a secret; a check fails any new doc step that does.
